issue.title: Proposal: track Ember
issue.body:
This proposes Ember as a tracked framework. CONTRIBUTING asks for an issue before a framework PR, so this is that issue. A draft PR follows.

## Setup

- `starter-ember`: the default app from [ember.nvp](https://github.com/NullVoxPopuli/ember.nvp), a Vite-based project generator. It uses template-tag (`.gjs`) components and `ember-source` 7.4.0.
- `app-ember`: the same generator with its `ssr` layer, which renders pages with [vite-ember-ssr](https://github.com/evoactivity/vite-ember-ssr) and rehydrates them in the browser. It has the same benchmark routes as the other apps.

Ember has a router link component (`<LinkTo>`), so `app-ember` also runs the SSR Router Link Load Test, with a plain-link copy of the table, the same as Next.js and React Router.

## Maintenance

@NullVoxPopuli maintains ember.nvp and will maintain this integration: version bumps, build or benchmark failures, and the methodology text.

comment.body: These 2 rehydration tests render a classic component. glimmer-workspace has no `testUnless`, so they use `skip`.
This fires in `init`, not when a subclass is defined. Code cannot detect a native `class extends Component`, and RFC 1117 covers `.extend()`. A subclass with no instances gets no warning.

issue.title: Fork results: Ember (ember.nvp), with and without SSR
issue.body:
Hi Nolan, thanks for publishing the harness and the raw results. I added Ember to a fork and ran it. All 85 Ember agents so far passed every test. With ember.nvp 2.1.1, Ember without SSR has a median cost of $3.02 over 10 agents. That is close to vanilla ($2.98) and below Next.js ($3.14), in the lower part of your table. Ember with SSR costs more than most frameworks. This post is the summary, with the latest run of each scenario. The comments have the details of each run and the follow-ups. ## Setup The fork is on [branch `ember-nvp`](https://github.com/NullVoxPopuli-ai-agent/agent-framework-benchmark/tree/ember-nvp). It adds three keys, with the same `SPEC.md` and tests: - `ember`: "Ember, starting from a project generated by ember.nvp (`npx ember.nvp`)" - `ember-ssr`: "Ember with server-side rendering, starting from a project generated by ember.nvp with its ssr layer (`npx ember.nvp --layers ssr`)" - `ember-cli`: "Ember, starting from a project generated by ember-cli (`npx ember-cli@latest new my-app`)". This is the command in the Ember guides, and it makes a client-side app only. [ember.nvp](https://github.com/NullVoxPopuli/ember.nvp) is a project generator for Ember on Vite. Ember has no official agent tooling, so `setup-tooling.sh` installs nothing for these keys. ## Results Opus 5.5 at `--effort=high`, 5 iterations per run, and 10 in run 9. The table has the best agent of each key over all runs: the agent with the lowest cost, which also used the fewest tokens. Your table has medians, so the bullets below compare medians. The tables list only tokens and cost. The runs used a shared Ryzen 9 7900X VM with rootless Podman. ## Where the tokens went (run 2, `ember`)

Each turn sends the whole context again, so I weighted each tool result by the number of turns after it.

| Work | Share of input |
| --- | ---: |
| `SPEC.md`, the tests, and the design files | 31% |
| Screenshots (about 23 images per run) | 22% |
| System prompt and tools | 17% |
| Writing app code | 12% |
| ember.nvp: `--help`, generation, reading its source | 5% |
| Listing `ember-source/dist` to find import paths | 4% |
| Builds, servers, test runs, other | 9% |

I expect the first three rows to be similar for every framework. Your results have no transcripts, so I could not check that.

The `ember-ssr` agents in run 2 read about twice as much tool output as the `ember` agents, mostly the vite-ember-ssr README and source. They needed to know how to set page titles and 404 status codes. Four of the 5 also replaced vite-ember-ssr's boot code, because it removed the `#hash` from the URL, and the spec has a `#moves` URL.

</details>

issue.title: README: page titles and 404 pages with the ssr layer
issue.body:
The README's ssr section now shows how to set page titles and how to answer `404` for a URL that has no page.

In a run of [agent-framework-benchmark](https://github.com/nolanlawson/agent-framework-benchmark), all 5 agents with the ssr layer read the vite-ember-ssr README and source to learn these two things. That reading is a large part of why those runs used about twice the tokens of the runs without the layer. All 5 agents found the same answers, and those answers are now in the README:

- Page titles: delete the static `<title>` from `index.html`. Some agents set `document.title` by hand. The README uses [ember-page-title](https://github.com/ember-cli/ember-page-title), with a one-line re-export of its service, because the app does not merge services from libraries. Without the re-export, the helper throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')`. With the static `<title>`, the HTML from the server has two titles, and the first one is the static title.
- 404: vite-ember-ssr answers `200`, or `500` if the render fails. A catch-all route marks its page with `data-not-found`, and `render()` in `server.js` answers `404` for it.

## Checks

I generated a JS app with `--layers ssr --ssr.mode server` from this branch, applied the README steps, built it, and ran `node server.js`:

| URL | Status | `<title>` |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `/` | 200 | `Docs App` (from the application template) |
| `/about` | 200 | `About \| Docs App` (one title) |
| `/nope` | 404 | `Docs App`, with "Page not found" in the body |

In Chrome, after rehydration, each page has one `<title>` with the same text. With the static `<title>` kept, the server HTML for `/about` has `Minimal App`, then `About | Docs App`.

`prettier --check README.md` passes.

## Possible follow-up

The layer could do these steps itself: delete the static `<title>`, and answer `404` in `server.js`. That changes generated files, so I kept it out of this PR.

issue.title: Join the reactivity report into the rows in one place
issue.body:
Joins the reactivity report into the property rows in ember-debug only. Part of the cleanup of emberjs/ember-inspector#2776. Needs the PR below it in the stack.

Before:

- ember-debug joined the report into the rows of the first send (`applyReactivityToProperties`).
- The inspector app did the same join again for each `updateReactivity` message. It guessed where the `args` dependent keys came from with `deps[0]?.name?.startsWith('@')`.
- Args had two shapes. They were dependent keys of the `args` row when the instance had an `args` property, and `@` rows when it did not.

After:

- ember-debug builds one row list, `reactivityRows`, for the first send and for each update.
- Every arg is a read-only `@` row with its value, its dependencies and its changed flag. The `args` row is a plain property again.
- `updateReactivity` sends `{ objectId, reactivity, rows }`. The app sets the fields of each row on the property row with the same name, and knows nothing about args.

This changes what the user sees. A Glimmer component now shows `@title` as a row, not as a dependent key under `args`. The description of #2776 needs that update when this merges.

Tests:

issue.body:
Gives every dependency tag one name in every list of the object inspector. Part of the cleanup of emberjs/ember-inspector#2776. Needs the PR below it in the stack.

Before, one pane named the same thing in different ways:

- An arg was `args.title` in the getter dependencies, and `@title` in the summary and the arg rows.
- An own property was `this.count` without the `tagFor` patch, and `ClassName.count` with it. So the name depended on the Ember version.

- own property of the inspected object: `this.count`
- named arg: `@title`
- property of another object: `ParentName.title`

Added in `f8f91ccf8f`. Under a non-classic route, `{{outlet}}` in a component now asserts:

> {{outlet}} in a component works only under a classic route. Render {{outlet}} in the route template, or pass @outlet={{@outlet}} to the component.

The keyword in `STRICT_MODE_KEYWORDS` only lets the compiled form `{{component (-outlet @outlet)}}` build in strict-mode templates. The list had `-outlet` before #21460. You can see it with `git show 4b5d79a6d7^:packages/@ember/template-compiler/lib/plugins/index.ts`.

`outletHelper` decides what renders:

- If `@outlet` is defined, the helper renders it. A route template or invokable has `@outlet` for every route manager.
- If not, the helper reads the dynamic scope. A classic level puts its child outlet there.
- A non-classic level puts a sentinel reference there. If the helper reads the sentinel, it asserts.

Before this commit, the outlet rendered nothing and gave no error. The test `{{outlet}} in a component asserts` uses `assert.rejectsAssertion`. It fails if the assertion is removed, and also if the non-classic level does not set the sentinel.

The five route-managers smoke scenarios pass. No smoke fixture triggers the assertion.
